fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. "Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?" (Ecclesiastes 7:16) The Teacher is asking a real question there. He's warning about going too far. I'll be honest, I read that and my hat tilted a little.

That's right. "Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins." (Ecclesiastes 7:20) The Teacher says it about everybody. And yes, that includes the guy who shows up with the perfect batch of cookies. That's me, and I'm sitting in that boat with you.

Yes, that's how he says it. The Teacher tested all this by wisdom and resolved to be wise, and then he says, "But it was beyond me." (Ecclesiastes 7:23) Wisdom still outran him. I think that's a humble thing to admit.

That's right. "What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?" (Ecclesiastes 7:24) Picture reaching down a well and your arm just runs out. That's the feeling the Teacher is putting into words. He asks the question out loud.
